1/1: First, the symptom is that in ```python foo = _undef bar ``` highlight.js is picking up the trailing “def” inside `_undef` plus the newline and `bar` as a function‐definition, so it splits `_undef` into `_un` + `def` and then highlights `bar` as a title.function. The root cause is that the “function-def” matcher in `python.js` is too permissive: match: [ /def/, /\s+/, IDENT_RE ] – it will happily match the “def” at the end of any identifier (or anywhere) so long as it is followed by whitespace and another identifier. We need to require word-boundaries around “def” so that only a standalone keyword is matched. Below is a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* patch to fix it in **src/languages/python.js**: ```javascript ### src/languages/python.js <<<<<<< SEARCH { match: [ /def/, /\s+/, IDENT_RE, ], scope: { 1: "keyword", 3: "title.function" }, contains: [ PARAMS ] }, ======= { match: [ /\bdef\b/, /\s+/, IDENT_RE, ], scope: { 1: "keyword", 3: "title.function" }, contains: [ PARAMS ] }, >>>>>>> REPLACE ``` This change ensures that only an isolated `def` (surrounded by word boundaries) will trigger the function‐definition rule and stops chopping identifiers like `_undef`.
